messages:
alex: Heads-up — after the recent kernel selector change we see a ~7% p99 tail increase on the 16xA100 TP+PP setup when serving long-context chat (8k+). Looks tied to KV cache behavior after the shard-routing tweak. :thinking:
mira: Can you paste the perf trace and the exact config used? TP/PP split + batch size?
alex: Config: TP=2, PP=4, DP=2, global_batch=48, per_gpu_batch=3. We switched from static round-robin KV shards -> dynamic hot-slice routing (route to owning shard unless cached remotely). Here's the simplified nvprof-ish slice showing time spent in all-reduce and recv/send windows:
```
# timeline (simplified):
compute:  120ms
allreduce: 45ms (blocked 30ms waiting for recv)
recv memcpy:  28ms (sequential across ranks)
cache lookup + deserialize: 5ms
```
alex: The curious bit — when requests have varying prefix lengths we see a surge in remote recv time, so cross-node transfer spikes for some tail cases.
sam: Yeah that pattern screams serialization/transfer amplification. Dynamic routing reduces redundant replication but increases network incidence for hot prefixes that cross TP boundaries. Did we try overlapping recv with compute (async copy + kernel prelaunch)?
mira: Are we using NCCL multi-threaded progress / CUDA IPC for intra-host? If not, that could explain the sequential recv windows.
tess: Also DP factor matters: with DP=2 we have two replicas; if hot slices are not replicated, both replicas may request the same remote shard causing duplicate transfers. Replicating the hottest N layers across DP replicas reduces network but increases memory. Tradeoff.
eng-monitor-bot: [trace] Serving trace 1898456721 — kv_miss_remote spikes at 2023-11-09T14:22:10Z (link: https://perf.redwood/traces/1898456721) :rotating_light:
jia: Quick numbers from microbench we ran this morning (16xA100):
- static per-layer shard (baseline): median latency 42ms, p99 110ms
- dynamic routing (current): median 40ms, p99 118ms
- hybrid (replicate top-3 hot layers + dynamic for rest): median 41ms, p99 106ms
jia: So hybrid seems to regain tail while keeping median close.
alex: Nice. Do we have per-layer heatmap of remote transfer counts? That helps decide which layers to replicate.
mira: I have a quick script that aggregates kv_miss_remote by layer from traces. Example output:
```
layer,remote_hits
0,1200
1,980
2,45
3,30
4,10
```
mira: Layers 0/1 are super hot for chat prefix reuse. Replicating them across DP replicas is cheap (small KV size) and avoids network jitter.
sam: Another lever: batching heuristics — group requests by prefix hash within small time windows so we hit local cache more often. That needs a short delay (5-15ms) but hugely reduces remote misses for high QPS tails. Worth experimenting.
tess: For TP vs PP nuance: if TP shards own different MLP weights but PP shards own contiguous layer blocks, then routing at layer granularity maps better to PP boundaries. For TP-heavy models (w/ weight sharding), hot KV may be evenly spread and replication gets costlier.
jia: Agreed. We should add two experiments: 1) hybrid replication top-K layers + dynamic routing for rest 2) micro-batching by prefix with 10ms hold + async recv overlap. Measure p50/p95/p99 and remote_bytes/s.
alex: Action items:
- mira: run per-layer heatmap for last 48h and push top-5 candidate layers.
- jia: schedule hybrid replication test on 16xA100 canary (non-prod) tomorrow.
- sam: prototype batching-by-prefix shim in runtime (10ms) and enable async copy/NCCL progressive recv.
- tess: add metric kv_miss_remote_per_replica and kv_remote_latency_breakdown.
mira: I'll also check if recent kernel-selector change disabled our cudaMemcpyAsync ordering — saw some ordering flags off in the new selector commit.
alex: If hybrid + batching regains tail we can default to hybrid on high-latency-sensitive customers and expose knobs in config.
jia: FYI cost tradeoff: replicating 2 layers across DP=2 adds ~3% GPU memory but cuts remote bandwidth by ~40% in our sim.
sam: One more note: check NCCL version — a regression in NCCL 2.x changed progress semantics for point-to-point which may explain the sequential recv behavior.
mira: I'll add NCCL and libcuda versions to the trace exports.
eng-monitor-bot: Noted actions assigned. :white_check_mark:
alex: Great thread. Let's reconvene after the canary runs. :eyes:
